verdict.rationale: Consensus's own Consensus Meter classifies each relevant paper as supporting, refuting, or mixed/inconclusive and displays the distribution, so analysts see agreement and disagreement rather than a single answer. The docs scope it to yes/no/possibly questions, which is a documented limitation, so coverage is partial. Per-response citations let users trace each claim to its source. Missing for 10: agreement/disagreement mapping for open-ended (non-yes/no) questions, explanation of why studies conflict, independent or hands-on corroboration of the meter's accuracy.

support.subject: As an analyst, I can see where sources agree and disagree instead of a single unqualified answer

citations.quote: The Consensus Meter is a visual aggregator that, for a yes/no/possibly question, classifies each relevant paper as supporting, refuting, or mixed/inconclusive, then displays the distribution.
Consensus Meter: aggregates per-study verdicts (Yes / No / Possibly / Mixed / Unknown) into a single distribution for a yes/no research question
Every response includes citations, so you can trace each insight back to the original source.
